newsitem.title: USA: Prodi says Clinton not negative on euro.
newsitem.headline: Prodi says Clinton not negative on euro.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Friday that U.S. President Bill Clinton did not view Europe's plans to launch a single European currency unfavourably.
"America absolutely does not look on the euro unfavourably," Produi told reporters at a late-night briefing. He added, "It is very interested."
"Clinton stressed that America has never looked with hostility at a strengthening of Europe," he added.
Prodi also said that Clinton believed the existence of a second currency with a key role in the international financial system would be very attractive.
"Having another currency sustaining the international monetary system is extremely useful," Prodi said.
He said the the present situation in which the monetary system weighed on a single currency was "excessive".
